Atomic Number (Z) : x The symbol of atomic number (Z) is a conventional symbol possibly came from the German word Atomzahl which means atomic number. x Atomic number of an element is the number of protons in the nucleus of its atom. x It is the characteristic of a chemical element and determines its place in the periodic table. x The atomic number of each element is certain and constant. x Atoms of diﬀ erent elements are with diﬀ erent atomic number. x The atomic number of Hydrogen is 1, it means it has one proton in its nucleus. Mass Number (A) : x (A) has been derived from German word Atomge which means atomic weight. x The total number of protons and neutrons in an atom’s nucleus is known as its mass number. x It determines the atomic mass of atoms. x A mass number of atom = No. of protons + No. of neutrons in nucleus of an atom. x It represents the total number of nucleons in the nucleus of an atom. x The mass number is not a fundamental character of the element. x An element may have atoms with diﬀ erent mass number. Atomic Weight : x The atomic weight of an atom is approximately equal to its mass number.  Atomic weight Mass number (A) Atomic weight No. of protons in nucleus + No. of neutrons in the nucleus. In an atom, the order of ﬁ lling up of the orbitals is governed by – (a) Aufbau's principle (b) Heisenberg's uncertainty principle (c) Hund's rule (d) Pauli's exclusion principle I.A.S. (Pre) 2001 Ans. (a) The Aufbau principle is used to determine the electron conﬁ guration of an atom, molecule or ion. The principle postulates a hypothetical process in which an atom is 'built up' by progressively adding electrons. As they are added, they assume their most stable condition (electron orbitals) with respect to the nucleus and those electrons already there. According to the principle, electrons ﬁ ll orbitals starting at the lowest available (possible) energy levels before ﬁ lling higher levels (e.g. 1s before 2s). 24.
